The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Civic building · 1883

    Austrian Parliament

    Theophil Hansen designed it in a classical style to recall the birthplace of democracy, and it was finished in 1883. Austria’s National Council and Federal Council meet inside.

    Look for

    Athena holds a small winged Victory in her hand; the reclining figures below stand for the rivers Danube, Inn, Elbe and Vltava.

  2. 02
    Palace · 1723

    Belvedere

    The Upper and Lower Belvedere were built in the early 1700s. The Austrian Gallery holds the largest Klimt collection, including The Kiss.

    Look for

    From the terrace of the Upper Belvedere, the gardens lead your eye down to the spire of St Stephen’s Cathedral.

  3. 03
    Palace · 1279

    Hofburg

    The imperial residence grew from a medieval castle into a complex of wings. The Spanish Riding School and the imperial apartments are inside.

    Look for

    The red, black and gold Swiss Gate from the 1550s leads into the oldest courtyard, the Swiss Court.

  4. 04
    Church · 1737

    Karlskirche

    Vowed during a plague in 1713 and dedicated to St Charles Borromeo. The oval dome and the spiral reliefs on the columns are the set piece.

    Look for

    In the pond in front sits Henry Moore’s bronze Hill Arches.

  5. 05
    Museum · 1891

    Kunsthistorisches Museum

    Opened in 1891 to house the imperial collections. Bruegel, Vermeer, and the Kunstkammer of curiosities are the reasons to stay.

    Look for

    Above the arches of the main staircase are paintings by the young Gustav Klimt, his brother Ernst and Franz Matsch.

  6. 06
    Museum · 1889

    Natural History Museum

    It opened in 1889 to house the imperial natural collections. Its best-known object is the Venus of Willendorf, around 30,000 years old.

    Look for

    Between the two museums, Maria Theresa sits on a high bronze throne, surrounded by her generals and advisers.

  7. 07
    Palace · 1780

    Schönbrunn

    Rebuilt in the 18th century for Maria Theresa, it has 1,441 rooms. The Gloriette on the hill looks back over the yellow facade.

  8. 08
    Church · 1433

    St. Stephen’s Cathedral

    A church has stood here since the 12th century. The south tower, the Steffl, was finished in 1433 and is still the city’s landmark.

    Look for

    Left of the main door, two iron bars set in the wall are old Viennese measures of length, used to check cloth sold in the market.

  9. 09
    Culture · 1869

    Vienna State Opera

    The original opened in 1869 and was mocked at first. It burned in 1945 and reopened in 1955.

    Look for

    In the loggia above the Ring, frescoes by Moritz von Schwind show scenes from Mozart’s The Magic Flute.
